_meta.purpose: Cross-project growing glossary of the JSON field names/shapes Gemini has actually used, across both directions: (a) analyzing a reference design into JSON, (b) analyzing a brand's own source images into JSON, (c) the final generation-prompt JSON sent back to Gemini. Load this in tools/parameter-visualizer.html — it grows every time a new analysis JSON is loaded there and you choose to merge new fields in.
_meta.how_to_extend: Open parameter-visualizer.html, load a new analysis/generation JSON, click 'Scan into vocabulary', review the diff, export, and commit the updated vocabulary.json here.

design_analysis_schema.description: Fields Gemini uses when asked to reverse-engineer an existing reference product design into JSON (the 'analyze the supplier's design' step).

dominant_landmark.description: The single largest/most central visual element.

position_pct.description: [x,y] as 0-100 percentages of frame, origin top-left

secondary_elements.description: Supporting elements, each with element + role (and sometimes position_pct).

filler_motif.description: The repeated texture/natural element used to fill space.

delight_element.description: Exactly ONE whimsical/non-geographic object that exists purely for charm.

nameplate.description: How the product/place name is physically constructed and where it sits.

integrated_with.description: What element the nameplate is physically attached to/part of — nameplates are almost never free-floating.

density_pct_frame_filled.description: Measured, not vibe-based — a key discovery: reference lines are consistently 85-95%, and generations that come back sparse are a precise measurable deviation from this, not a vague aesthetic complaint.

what_is_deliberately_omitted.description: What a literal photo would include that the design deliberately leaves out — e.g. human figures, in every reference example found so far.

human_figures_present.description: HARD RULE discovered across the La Salle project's 4 reference examples: always false. Worth checking explicitly on every new reference line rather than assuming.

brand_extraction_schema.description: Fields used when analyzing the TARGET BRAND's own real source images (a building, a product, a cultural motif) — same rigor as design_analysis_schema, applied to the new brand instead of the reference. Schema varies more by subject matter than the design-analysis schema does; these are examples per subject type, not one fixed shape.

overall_form.example: Single curved tower, convex facade, no straight-line sections

ground_floor_treatment.description: Exclude signage/text/logos from this description entirely — naming them still invites the model to reproduce them later.

distinguishing_silhouette_features.description: The 2-4 things that make THIS instance recognizable vs. a generic version of the same category.

edge_technique.description: Be very specific about surface/texture, not generic '3D render' language.

hardware.description: VERIFY placement/position against a second reference photo — an extraction placed a knob on the wrong face in one project, caught only by cross-checking.

dimensions_cm.description: VERIFY against a spec-sheet/label if one is visible in any reference photo — an extraction was off by ~40% in one project.

abstractable_motifs.description: Geometric/symbolic elements that could be extracted WITHOUT reproducing any human figures present.

figures_present_not_to_reproduce.description: Explicitly name what NOT to carry forward, so a later generation prompt can exclude it by name.

generation_prompt_schema.description: The final JSON sent AS the literal generation prompt (Controlled Generation) — merges a populated design-analysis-shaped object with brand-extraction data, plus generation-specific control fields.

action.description: Community convention, not a real Gemini API field — just a strong signal to the model that this whole JSON is a literal instruction set.

output_type.description: State explicitly whether the deliverable is a flat print-ready illustration or a photorealistic product photograph — these are different requests and asking for one when the other is needed produces a technically-fine WRONG deliverable.

subject.description: Community-convention key grouping what should be depicted.

visual_style.description: Community-convention key for line/color/density/perspective/texture/edge-treatment rules — best populated FROM a design_analysis_schema extraction, not invented.

bbox.description: Fractional, origin top-left — the 'JSON as layout map' community technique.

layer.description: Optional z-order hint, e.g. 'dominant landmark', 'distant background'.

note.description: Used for a reserved/calm zone instruction, e.g. a logo pocket to leave uncluttered.

hard_exclusions.description: Absolute negative constraints, most effective when the excluded thing was never shown/named in an attached reference image either — describing a forbidden thing still invites it.

_source / _correction / _why prefixed ke.description: House convention introduced in this project: prefix an explanatory key with an underscore to record provenance or a manual correction inline in the JSON itself, without it being mistaken for an actual generation instruction. Gemini appears to ignore underscore-prefixed keys as instructions while still 'reading' them as context — unverified assumption, worth testing directly if it ever matters.
